Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost breakdown were really helpful. Before we move to a formal pilot, procurement needs clarity on two things for our legal and finance teams:

1) If we upgrade from Compact to Throughput mid-contract, how are the previously purchased Compact seats/credits handled? Is there a pro-rata conversion or credit?
2) If we need to step down later (throughput -> compact), do we get stepdown credits or is that treated as forfeiture?
3) Any constraints around feature bundles (e.g., A/B evaluation tooling and Optimize add-on) being locked to a tier? Can we mix features across tiers during a pilot?

Attached is our internal procurement checklist — can you review and call out any redlines we should expect?

Thanks,

Hi Lindsey — great question and the right things to lock down before pilot kickoff. I pulled together the short answers below and attached a one-page conversion matrix for your legal/finance team. Quick summary:

- Upgrade (Compact -> Throughput): we apply remaining Compact credit value as a one-time conversion credit toward the Throughput commitment. Conversion uses a published seat-to-throughput multiplier (attached) and prorates by remaining contract term.
- Stepdown (Throughput -> Compact): we offer a stepdown allowance but it depends on contract class. Standard self-serve contracts: no retroactive credits (forfeiture). Enterprise reserved/Dedicated: we include a stepdown buffer (typically 20% of committed throughput) and a defined credit schedule if the change is requested at least 30 days before renewal.
- Feature bundling: Optimize and A/B evaluation tooling can be added as add-ons during a pilot. They are not strictly locked to a tier for pilots under 6 months; for annual reserved commitments we recommend bundling them into the package for predictable pricing and feature SLAs.

What I attached: Redwood-Pack-Options-v2.pdf (one-page conversion table) and HS_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (filled with next steps).

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll loop in Lauren for the exact wording we recommend in SOWs for stepdown allowances (so legal sees precise language).
2) Ben will size an illustrative conversion example using your expected 3-month pilot usage and proposed start date.
3) We can put a provisional clause in the SOW that defines the conversion multiplier and the 30-day timing for stepdown credit eligibility.

If that sounds right I'll produce a redline-friendly clause and a short pricing addendum for your procurement team.

Best,

Lindsey — adding a few technical/operational notes to Marcus's commercial summary so your engineering and procurement teams are aligned:

- Autoscale burst vs committed throughput: burst capacity (ephemeral GPU autoscale) isn't converted or credited. Only committed throughput or pre-purchased seat credits are eligible for conversion.
- Quantized model licensing: if you switch to a quantized variant for cost reasons, we treat it as the same model family for conversion purposes unless you opt for a different SLA class.
- Feature gating during pilots: we'll enable Optimize and the A/B evaluation feature flags in a sandboxed environment tied to your pilot account. That means you can mix features across tiers for up to 90 days; after that we recommend adopting the features into the chosen tier for support continuity.

I've drafted suggested SOW language below that Marcus can fold into the pricing addendum — short, contract-friendly text that legal usually accepts.

--- suggested SOW excerpt ---
Stepdown and Upgrade Credits: Customer may request an upgrade or downgrade to their active package. Upgrades are eligible for an account credit equal to the prorated value of remaining seat credits, converted via Redwood's published conversion multiplier. Downgrades are subject to the stepdown schedule negotiated in the Order Form; for Reserved Capacity agreements a defined stepdown credit schedule applies if changes are requested >=30 days prior to renewal. Burst capacity and ephemeral autoscale are excluded from conversion credits.
--- end excerpt ---

Happy to redline language or expand the excerpt for legal.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
